page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Intel-based N2 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.8 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES cryptography, and Intel Speed Select technology.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates moderate memory performance but limited raw compute throughput. The Passmark memory score and single-threaded gzip compression both rank in the average tier. However, most compute-bound benchmarks, including stress-ng, Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, and Passmark CPU suites, fall into the bottom 25 percent of tested hardware. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and small-model LLM prompt processing show lower relative performance, landing in the bottom 10 percent. Database operations and Redis SET performance also register in the lower quartile, reflecting the trade-off between high memory capacity and modest processing power.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-4 offers a specialized resource profile that prioritizes memory density over high-performance compute. This makes it a qualitatively cost-effective option for workloads that require a larger memory footprint without demanding intensive CPU cycles. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications such as caching layers, small-scale database hosting, enterprise application servers, and moderate web serving tasks where memory capacity is the primary bottleneck.
